summary.text: In his NTIA remarks, Cassady expressed a desire for U.S.-led AI to power the future of work, recreation, and life. On October 29, 2025, he described AI and 6G as mutually reinforcing technologies and called AI-driven networks essential for future competitiveness. On April 16, 2026, he described AI alongside other emerging technologies as part of a transformation that would fundamentally reorder the global economy.

Artificial intelligence, advanced semiconductors, quantum computing, biotechnology, autonomy, robotics, related critical infrastructure, and next-generation telecommunications will shape productivity, military power, supply chains, and global standards for decades to come.

statements.text: The Bureau of Cyberspace and Digital Policy – or CDP – plays a central role in aligning our diplomacy with our economic and security priorities. CDP works across the interagency and with America’s allies to secure supply chains, promote trusted technology, defend an open and interoperable Internet, and ensure international standards reflect democratic values and free enterprise principles.

statements.text: Adam Cassady was appointed Ambassador at Large for Cyberspace and Digital Policy at the U.S. Department of State on August 7, 2026. He took his oath of office and assumed his duties on August 24, 2026. In this capacity, he advances U.S. leadership abroad in critical and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), autonomy, quantum, biotechnology, telecommunications, next generation communications, related critical infrastructure, and export diplomacy related to these topics.
